chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But upon those who take him as their guardian.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/master

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's authority (sulṭān) is not absolute over all believers but conditional upon their acceptance of his guidance, a nuance that distinguishes between general human susceptibility and specific spiritual subjugation. This explanation reinforces the Shia doctrine of free will, asserting that while Satan can influence those who follow him, he holds no dominion over the sincere servants of God who remain steadfast in faith.
